title: A Bear Hunt Adventure
strapline: Swishy grass, squelchy mud, a deep cold river — we're going on an adventure.
intent: A journey-and-obstacles adventure gives children a repeating structure to chant, predict and join in with their whole bodies.
Squelching through mud, splashing through water and stumbling through the forest is rich sensory and physical play.
The 'we can't go over it, we can't go under it' pattern builds positional language and problem-solving.
Making our own map and route sequences the journey and invents a shared story.
The scary-but-safe ending — the run home — lets children feel and manage excitement and mild fear together.
implementation: Build an obstacle journey with real textures — long grass, a mud tray, a water splash, a dark 'cave' den — to travel through.
Chant the repeating rhythm together as you go: 'We can't go over it, we can't go under it — we've got to go through it!'
Add the sound effects — swishy swashy, squelch squerch, splash splosh — and invite children to invent their own.
Wonder aloud at each obstacle: 'How will we get through this one? Over, under, or straight through?'
Make a map of the adventure together, drawing each place along the way.
Let the excitement build to the run home — a safe, thrilling ending everyone can join.
key_questions: How shall we get past this — over, under, or through?
What sound does the mud make when we squelch through it?
What might we find at the end of the adventure?
Which way did we come — can you remember the route?
How does your body feel when we run home?

impact.text: Children chant the repeating rhythm and use positional language along the way.
Children travel through varied textures and obstacles with confident whole-body movement.
Children invent sound effects and add their own ideas to the journey.
Children map and sequence the route and recount the adventure.
Children share the excitement and manage the thrill of the run home together.

enhancements: A real sensory obstacle trail — long grass, a mud patch, a water tray, a dark den — to travel through outdoors.
A big floor map to draw the route and mark each obstacle.
A sound-effects table with materials for swishing, squelching and splashing.
A cosy 'cave' den at the end with a torch and something to discover.
Wellies, coats and binoculars for kitting out the explorers.

playing_exploring: Children plunge into the mud, water and long grass, exploring textures with their whole bodies.
They chase the adventure wherever it leads, inventing new obstacles.
active_learning: Children keep going through every obstacle to reach the end of the journey.
They rise to the excitement of the run home and manage the thrill.
creating_thinking: Children work out how to get past each obstacle — over, under or through.
They map the route and invent their own sound effects and story turns.
